text:
Buffalo spent the first period piling up chances and had nothing to show for it on the scoreboard. The Sabres out-chanced Chicago 2.08 to 0.65 in expected goals over those 20 minutes, yet trailed 2-0 after Ryan Donato and Tyler Bertuzzi scored on shots with an 18 percent and a 6 percent chance of going in. Jack Quinn answered late in the period on a 5 percent look, the least likely goal of the night, and the comeback was on.

From there the game tightened. Tage Thompson tipped one in early in the second to tie it, and Oliver Moore put Chicago back up with 1:42 left in the period. Expected goals were nearly even in the second (CHI 0.85, BUF 0.80) and the third (CHI 1.12, BUF 1.05), so the two teams played the final 40 minutes close to level. Chicago's best chance of the night, a 39 percent look for Jordan Greenway in the third, went off target.

Buffalo finished it with two snap shots. Rasmus Dahlin tied it at 3-3 at 6:10 of the third, and Jiri Kulich won it at 13:20. Over the full game, BUF held a 3.93 to 2.61 edge in expected goals and a 64 to 38 edge in shot attempts, and a simulated replay of every shot gives the Sabres a 71 percent chance to win. That is the gap between how the game was played and how close it felt: Buffalo deserved this one, and had to come from two goals down to take it.
